wolfram.note: Stirling(n, Range(1,n)) with symbolic n leaks an internal Map/Function/Block threading scaffold into the result instead of staying unevaluated like Wolfram's StirlingS2(n, Range(1,n)) — Range(1,n) can't concretize for symbolic n, and the Listable-threading machinery doesn't recognize that and fall back cleanly. Likely a generic Listable/unresolved-Range interaction, not specific to Stirling; out of scope to chase into the engine's threading machinery from this lane.

sage.note: Both decline: compute-engine leaves Stirling(10, -5) unevaluated since a negative k is outside its textbook domain, and Sage's stirling_number2 raises OverflowError trying to convert -5 to an unsigned long.
sympy.note: Both decline: compute-engine leaves Stirling(10, -5) symbolic, as Wolfram does, and SymPy's stirling fails on a negative k.
julia.note: A negative k is outside Stirling's textbook domain, so compute-engine leaves it symbolic; Combinatorics.jl's stirlings2 extends past it and answers 0.
